In summary, our research is concerned with

the following problem: given an object category, how to obtain a compact, low dimensional representation of the features, while simultaneously ensuring that the resulting features are invariant to changes in scale, illumination and viewpoint?

developing a new framework for obtaining local feature descriptors which are invariant with respect to viewpoint, illumination, and scale, while at the same time being discriminative with respect to different object classes.

the development of novel methods for object recognition in real-life situations, where the objects are not necessarily rigid, the images are not always taken from a single viewpoint and the objects may be occluded by other objects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sMDS approach outperforms the other methods on the majority of the experiments, while it is also the most robust to the choice of the parameters.

the proposed sMDS framework provides a new and general framework for obtaining more distinctive local features by projecting the feature descriptors into low dimensionality while incorporating class information, and that the resulting feature representation is more suitable for object recognition.
the proposed approach to low dimensional feature representation is a very effective and powerful tool for improving the accuracy of object recognition.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a general method to improve local invariant feature representations, which is applicable in a wide range of computer vision problems.
we have shown that it is possible to obtain more discriminative local features by incorporating also class information into the representation.
we propose a new approach for learning class specific low dimensional representation of local features, which can be used to obtain more discriminative features for object recognition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
by combining class information with the original local features, we can obtain a more discriminative representation of the features.
by incorporating class information in a low dimensional embedding, the features become more discriminative.
the combination of local invariant features with class information is beneficial for viewpoint invariant object recognition.
